claims.text: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km — 18.0 km — over a booked optimal of 10.0 km on the trip record, an excess of 8.0 km and 80% of optimal. Both establishment gates in POL-RD-01 are cleared: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The rider's claim that the completed route went much farther than the closure required is therefore made out on the trace, not on the rider's characterisation of the trip.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip identifiers and pickup/start timestamps match across trip_record (TRP-09113, requested 18:12, started 18:20), gps_trace (first fix 18:20:00, last fix 18:54:00) and fare_breakdown (TRP-09113, charged 18:54:03), and the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden has now shifted to the driver to name a specific artifact and a specific clause; a general assertion that the closure forced the route does not discharge it beyond the capped exoneration measured below.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval with zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds across 100% coverage, so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires: no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds. No independent corroboration substitute is required and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is not open.

The driver is entitled to exoneration for the closure, but only up to the cap POL-RD-03 imposes. The LTA advisory names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, which the booked optimal route traverses (optimal_route_source records that segment), its validity window 18:14–18:55 overlaps the trip window, and the shortest lawful alternative was 12.0 km. The justified excess is therefore min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.6 km. The remaining 4.4 km of measured excess is not exonerated and falls to be refunded.

The driver cannot escape the cap by pointing to the rider's chat message. The only rider message on the record — 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion' — is a passive acknowledgement of the driver's own closure notice, names no road or place, and carries waypoint_hint null. Under POL-RD-04 the corroboration test is undecidable on that record and the clause is unavailable, so the 4.4 km of excess beyond the POL-RD-03 cap is not attributable to any rider instruction and is not excluded from the refund.

The refund is arithmetic. Because POL-RD-03 excuses only 3.6 km, POL-RD-02 runs against the closure-adjusted optimal route: 13.6 km and 27.2 minutes (booked 20.0 minutes scaled by 13.6/10.0, no amended duration being stored). Recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.6 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0, taken from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP on the optimal route = 23.416. Refund = 31.42 charged less 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05. That is 25.5% of charged_total: above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a partial refund of 8.05 — exactly the amount the rider contested.

For transparency, and to keep the arithmetic honest, the 2.80 SGD charged at the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is an off-optimal-route line (on_optimal_route false) and is itemised here rather than added: under POL-RD-09(1) off-route ERP is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because that refund is charged_total less a recomputed fare carrying only the on-route gantry. It is not added on top of the 8.05. The rider's recovery on this trip is 8.05, not 10.85.

The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is run on this trip and produces no pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610, so neither limb of the pattern test is met and no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) arises. The remedy is therefore the POL-RD-02 partial figure of 8.05, which is the figure the rider asks the tribunal to award.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and a monetary ruling, not a hold, is the right disposal. The trip identifiers match, the timestamps agree, the trace is unimpaired, the advisory is present and covers the window, every charge line on the fare breakdown has a counterpart in the trace (both ERP gantries are matched within the 250 m radius, the nearest fixes being 834 m and 223 m), and the computed refund of 8.004 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total. There is nothing here for a human reviewer to resolve that the arithmetic does not already resolve.

The outcome is a rider win on this record. The dispute is filed by the RIDER, fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so a PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05 under POL-GEN-03 returns part of the contested amount to the filing party and stops the rider carrying the unexonerated 4.4 km of the driver's route.

claims.text: The closure the rider herself accepts is documented, and it clears the first 3.60 km of excess on the driver's side. LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 is a HIGH-severity CLOSURE of the 'Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector' — the very segment the booking-time optimal route traverses, as the trip record's optimal_route_source confirms ('routing-engine-v3.2 snapshot 2026-09-20 18:12 SGT via Pelton Canal Link, the segment named in the LTA advisory'). The advisory runs 18:14–18:55 and so brackets the trip window of 18:20–18:54 well inside the 15-minute buffer POL-RD-03 allows at each end, and the completed trace leaves the closed corridor and rejoins it. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is the lesser of the measured 8.0 km and 1.30 x (12.0 km shortest lawful alternative - 10.0 km booked optimal) + 1.00 km tolerance = 3.60 km. So 3.60 km of the excess is exonerated as an external event and is not the driver's to refund.

The rider's recovery is the arithmetic refund against the closure-adjusted optimal route, not against the booked 10.0 km route. POL-RD-03 sets the closure-adjusted optimal at 10.0 + 3.60 = 13.60 km, with duration scaled to 27.2 minutes, and POL-RD-02 then gives recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP for the on-optimal-route Pelton gantry = 23.416, against a charged_total of 31.42. The refund is therefore 8.004, payable 8.05 after rounding up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is the ceiling of the rider's recovery on this record. An unadjusted computation against the booked optimal would produce 12.75 and is the wrong baseline on this evidence.

The 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' ERP line, flagged on_optimal_route false, is already comprehended inside that 8.05 refund and must never be added on top of it. POL-RD-02 recomputes the fare including only the gantries lying on the optimal route, and the only such line here is the 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' charge, which the recomputed fare of 23.416 already carries; the 3.80 total ERP billed against a 1.00 on-route pass-through is precisely where the difference sits. POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting an off-route pass-through a second time, so the rider cannot come away with 8.05 plus 2.80.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern on this driver and therefore no uplift. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610, which satisfies neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test — not '3 or more flags', and not the 0.05 ratio with at least 40 trips. Those two fields are the only ones POL-RD-06 permits for this test, and neither supports escalation to the FULL_REFUND remedy or the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral; the rider's remedy stays at the POL-RD-02 partial figure of 8.05.

The rider authorised the diversion as it happened. The chat log records the driver messaging at 18:22:40, two minutes into the trip, that the Pelton Canal Link closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop, and the rider replying at 18:23:10, 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion' — an instruction from the rider, in the chat log, inside the three minutes after the vehicle left the optimal corridor that POL-RD-04 allows. I disclose that the rider named no road and the message carries no waypoint_hint, so the 200 m waypoint-corroboration limb of POL-RD-04 cannot be run on this record; the exchange is relied on as the rider's authorisation of the diversion the driver had just identified, which is why the industrial-loop routing cannot be treated as the driver's unilateral choice.

The driver has discharged the burden POL-RD-08 places on him once the rider shows an excess: he points to a specific artifact and a specific clause — traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 and POL-RD-03 — rather than a general assertion that traffic was bad. The advisory names the road, carries an ID, overlaps the trip window and matches a route that leaves and rejoins the optimal corridor, which is exactly what POL-RD-08 requires. The excess is also stable and admissible: the governing figure is the trace distance of 18.0 km under POL-RD-01, the trace is at full weight with no gaps, so the 3.60 km cap does not move and the rider cannot inflate the measured excess beyond it.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — the route did deviate, the closure explains only part of it, and the arithmetic is set out line by line below.

DOES THE ROUTE DEVIATE? Yes. The governing measurement under POL-RD-01 is the trace distance on EV-GPS-09113, 18.0 km, against the booked optimal of 10.0 km on EV-TRIP-09113 — an excess of 8.0 km and 80% of optimal. Both establishment gates are cleared (over 20% and over 0.8 km), and 80% also makes the deviation MATERIAL. The trace is at full weight: 205 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, so it is NOT impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and the POL-RD-10(3) route is not open. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: trip id and timestamps match across EV-TRIP-09113, EV-GPS-09113 and EV-FARE-09113.

THE CLOSURE — EXONERATION IS CAPPED. The driver is right that the LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-09113-01, a HIGH-severity CLOSURE of the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector) covers this trip: it names the segment the booked optimal route traverses, its 18:14–18:55 window brackets the 18:20–18:54 trip, and the completed route leaves and rejoins the corridor. But POL-RD-03 exonerates only up to its cap: min(8.0 km measured, 1.30 × (12.0 − 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.6 km. The remaining 4.4 km of excess is not excused and stands against the driver.

THE RIDER'S CHAT MESSAGE DOES NOT CHANGE THAT. 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion' does not engage POL-RD-04: it names no road and carries waypoint_hint null, so the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable on this record, and the 4.4 km beyond the cap is not excluded as rider-requested.

REFUND (POL-RD-02). Against the closure-adjusted optimal route of 10.0 + 3.6 = 13.6 km, duration 20.0 × 13.6/10.0 = 27.2 min: recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 13.6 + 0.28 × 27.2) × 1.0 surge (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-09113) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP on the adjusted optimal route = 23.416. Charged total = 31.42. Refund = 31.42 − 23.416 = 8.004, rounded UP to SGD 8.05 (25.5% of the charge — above the 0.50 de minimis, below the 90% full-refund share, so PARTIAL_REFUND, not FULL_REFUND).

ERP (POL-RD-09). The 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is off the adjusted optimal route (on_optimal_route false) and is already comprehended inside the 8.05 — it must NEVER be added on top, so the rider's recovery is 8.05, not 10.85. The 1.00 Pelton gantry is the platform-classified on-optimal-route line and is carried inside the recomputed fare.

DRIVER PROFILE (POL-RD-06). The check was run: deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 610. Neither limb of the pattern test is met, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires either — identifiers and timestamps match, the trace is unimpaired, the advisory is present and covers the window, every charge line has a counterpart, and the refund is far under both SGD 150.00 and charged_total.

Confidence is 0.9, capped by the minimum weight (1.0) of the artifacts carrying the deciding facts — EV-TRIP-09113, EV-GPS-09113, EV-FARE-09113 and EV-ADVIS-09113-01, all at full weight.

Outcome: a partial refund of SGD 8.05 to the rider; the charge otherwise stands.

The driver is exonerated only up to the cap: min(8.0, 1.30 × (12.0 − 10.0) + 1.0) = 3.60 km. The remaining excess stands against the driver.

The 2.80 charged at the off-route 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is already comprehended inside the 8.05 and is NOT added on top of it (POL-RD-09(1)); it is itemised for transparency only. ruling.explanation:
This trip is a material route deviation; the argument is only over how much of it the road closure excuses, and over one ERP line that should never have been charged.

DISTANCE. Under POL-RD-01 the GPS trace governs, not the trip record's rounded copy: 18.0 km driven against a booked optimal of 10.0 km is an excess of 8.0 km, or 80% of optimal. Both establishment gates pass and the materiality threshold is crossed, so the deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The driver's and the rider's submissions agree on this and are accepted.

CLOSURE. LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 (HIGH severity, Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, valid 18:14–18:55) names the segment the booked optimal used, brackets the trip window and matches a route that leaves and rejoins the corridor. Under POL-RD-03 it excuses only the capped amount: min(8.0, 1.30 × (12.0 − 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km. The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 13.60 km and 27.2 minutes, and the remaining 4.4 km of excess is not excused. Both the driver's and the rider's figures on this point are accepted.

RIDER'S CHAT. “Understood, please take the lawful diversion” names no road or place and carries no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and that clause is unavailable. I therefore reject the driver's submission that the message excuses more than the closure cap already does: it is an acknowledgement of the driver's own closure notice, not a rider-requested detour. The rider's matching submission is accepted on the same ground.

REFUND. Because POL-RD-03 excuses only 3.60 km, POL-RD-02 runs against the closure-adjusted optimal: recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 13.60 + 0.28 × 27.2) × 1.0 surge multiplier (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP on the optimal route = SGD 23.416, against a charged total of SGD 31.42. Refund = SGD 8.004, payable SGD 8.05 after rounding up. The SGD 2.80 “Industrial loop exit” line is off the optimal route and is already comprehended in that figure under POL-RD-09(1); both sides are right that it is itemised, not added again.

BILLING INTEGRITY. The two submissions that “both ERP gantries are matched within the 250 m radius” are rejected. Matching compares the gantry's coordinates against the trace, treating a fix within 250 m as a crossing, and the closest the trace ever comes to the SGD 1.00 “Pelton lawful diversion entry” gantry is 834 m (fix 13, 18:22:10) — no fix is within 250 m, so the trace never passes it. POL-RD-09(4) makes that a billing-integrity failure: the SGD 1.00 is refunded in full as a standalone correction and is referred below. This is why the total is SGD 9.05 rather than the SGD 8.05 claimed. The second gantry (223 m) is matched and is dealt with through the POL-RD-02 arithmetic. POL-RD-10(8) is not triggered, because the only unmatched line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4).

DRIVER PROFILE. POL-RD-06 is run because the deviation is material: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days, so neither limb of the pattern test is met. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral arises. Both submissions on this point are accepted.

NO ESCALATION. POL-RD-10 is not engaged: the trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, the trace is unimpaired (205 fixes, 10-second interval, no gaps over 90s), the advisory covers the window, and the refund is far below the SGD 150 ceiling.

OUTCOME. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.05 to the rider — SGD 8.05 on the route-deviation computation plus the SGD 1.00 billing correction. No driver compensation is due.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 1.00 “Pelton lawful diversion entry” ERP line on trip TRP-09113 was charged for a gantry the GPS trace never passes (closest fix 834 m, outside the 250 m match radius). The line is refunded in full as a standalone correction and the gantry-charging record for this trip should be reviewed.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: the deviation is established on this trip's own evidence, so the rider's starting point is right. The governing figure is the GPS trace distance, 18.0 km, against the booked optimal of 10.0 km on the trip record — 8.0 km of excess, 80% of optimal and material (POL-RD-01). Both parties agree on that, and the rider's POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-08 claims are accepted: identifiers and start times match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and the burden shifts to the driver. The closure excuses the driver only up to the cap. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-09113-01) names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, which the booked optimal route uses; its 18:14–18:55 window brackets the trip; and the driven route leaves and rejoins the corridor. POL-RD-03 caps the justified excess at min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km, giving a closure-adjusted optimal of 13.60 km and 27.2 minutes; both advocates' POL-RD-03 claims are accepted. The remaining 4.4 km is the driver's. The driver's rider-authorisation argument fails. The only rider message, 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion', names no road or place and carries no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable; the 4.4 km is not excluded as rider-caused. The rider's POL-RD-04 claim is accepted and the driver's is rejected. The refund is arithmetic (POL-RD-02), run against the closure-adjusted route on the METERED model, with the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown: charged_total SGD 31.42; recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-route ERP = SGD 23.416; refund SGD 8.004, payable SGD 8.05. That is 25.5% of the charge — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90% full-refund share. Both advocates' POL-RD-02 figures are accepted, and the SGD 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' ERP line is off-route and already comprehended in the 8.05 under POL-RD-09(1), not added on top, as the rider correctly argues. One thing both advocates missed: the rider asserts both ERP gantries are matched within the 250 m radius, but that is wrong on its own figures — the 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' gantry sits 834 m from the nearest fix, well outside the 250 m match radius, while the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is 223 m away and is matched. The SGD 1.00 charged for the Pelton gantry is therefore a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes; under POL-RD-09(4) it is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a billing-integrity finding. It is not an escalation: POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes a line refunded under POL-RD-09(4). No repeat-deviation pattern exists — deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days — so there is no POL-RD-06(b) uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral; both advocates' POL-RD-06 claims are accepted. All artifacts relied on carry weight 1.0 and none is impaired, so no discount applies. Outcome: SGD 8.05 under POL-RD-02 plus SGD 1.00 under POL-RD-09(4) — a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.05 to the rider. ledger.claim: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km — 18.0 km — over a booked optimal of 10.0 km on the trip record, an excess of 8.0 km and 80% of optimal. Both establishment gates in POL-RD-01 are cleared: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The rider's claim that the completed route went much farther than the closure required is therefore made out on the trace, not on the rider's characterisation of the trip.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip identifiers and pickup/start timestamps match across trip_record (TRP-09113, requested 18:12, started 18:20), gps_trace (first fix 18:20:00, last fix 18:54:00) and fare_breakdown (TRP-09113, charged 18:54:03), and the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden has now shifted to the driver to name a specific artifact and a specific clause; a general assertion that the closure forced the route does not discharge it beyond the capped exoneration measured below.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval with zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds across 100% coverage, so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires: no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds. No independent corroboration substitute is required and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is not open.

The driver is entitled to exoneration for the closure, but only up to the cap POL-RD-03 imposes. The LTA advisory names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, which the booked optimal route traverses (optimal_route_source records that segment), its validity window 18:14–18:55 overlaps the trip window, and the shortest lawful alternative was 12.0 km. The justified excess is therefore min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.6 km. The remaining 4.4 km of measured excess is not exonerated and falls to be refunded.

The driver cannot escape the cap by pointing to the rider's chat message. The only rider message on the record — 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion' — is a passive acknowledgement of the driver's own closure notice, names no road or place, and carries waypoint_hint null. Under POL-RD-04 the corroboration test is undecidable on that record and the clause is unavailable, so the 4.4 km of excess beyond the POL-RD-03 cap is not attributable to any rider instruction and is not excluded from the refund.

The refund is arithmetic. Because POL-RD-03 excuses only 3.6 km, POL-RD-02 runs against the closure-adjusted optimal route: 13.6 km and 27.2 minutes (booked 20.0 minutes scaled by 13.6/10.0, no amended duration being stored). Recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.6 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0, taken from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP on the optimal route = 23.416. Refund = 31.42 charged less 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05. That is 25.5% of charged_total: above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a partial refund of 8.05 — exactly the amount the rider contested.

For transparency, and to keep the arithmetic honest, the 2.80 SGD charged at the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is an off-optimal-route line (on_optimal_route false) and is itemised here rather than added: under POL-RD-09(1) off-route ERP is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because that refund is charged_total less a recomputed fare carrying only the on-route gantry. It is not added on top of the 8.05. The rider's recovery on this trip is 8.05, not 10.85.

The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is run on this trip and produces no pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610, so neither limb of the pattern test is met and no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) arises. The remedy is therefore the POL-RD-02 partial figure of 8.05, which is the figure the rider asks the tribunal to award.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and a monetary ruling, not a hold, is the right disposal. The trip identifiers match, the timestamps agree, the trace is unimpaired, the advisory is present and covers the window, every charge line on the fare breakdown has a counterpart in the trace (both ERP gantries are matched within the 250 m radius, the nearest fixes being 834 m and 223 m), and the computed refund of 8.004 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total. There is nothing here for a human reviewer to resolve that the arithmetic does not already resolve.

The outcome is a rider win on this record. The dispute is filed by the RIDER, fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so a PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05 under POL-GEN-03 returns part of the contested amount to the filing party and stops the rider carrying the unexonerated 4.4 km of the driver's route.

The closure the rider herself accepts is documented, and it clears the first 3.60 km of excess on the driver's side. LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 is a HIGH-severity CLOSURE of the 'Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector' — the very segment the booking-time optimal route traverses, as the trip record's optimal_route_source confirms ('routing-engine-v3.2 snapshot 2026-09-20 18:12 SGT via Pelton Canal Link, the segment named in the LTA advisory'). The advisory runs 18:14–18:55 and so brackets the trip window of 18:20–18:54 well inside the 15-minute buffer POL-RD-03 allows at each end, and the completed trace leaves the closed corridor and rejoins it. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is the lesser of the measured 8.0 km and 1.30 x (12.0 km shortest lawful alternative - 10.0 km booked optimal) + 1.00 km tolerance = 3.60 km. So 3.60 km of the excess is exonerated as an external event and is not the driver's to refund.

The rider's recovery is the arithmetic refund against the closure-adjusted optimal route, not against the booked 10.0 km route. POL-RD-03 sets the closure-adjusted optimal at 10.0 + 3.60 = 13.60 km, with duration scaled to 27.2 minutes, and POL-RD-02 then gives recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP for the on-optimal-route Pelton gantry = 23.416, against a charged_total of 31.42. The refund is therefore 8.004, payable 8.05 after rounding up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is the ceiling of the rider's recovery on this record. An unadjusted computation against the booked optimal would produce 12.75 and is the wrong baseline on this evidence.

The 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' ERP line, flagged on_optimal_route false, is already comprehended inside that 8.05 refund and must never be added on top of it. POL-RD-02 recomputes the fare including only the gantries lying on the optimal route, and the only such line here is the 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' charge, which the recomputed fare of 23.416 already carries; the 3.80 total ERP billed against a 1.00 on-route pass-through is precisely where the difference sits. POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting an off-route pass-through a second time, so the rider cannot come away with 8.05 plus 2.80.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern on this driver and therefore no uplift. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610, which satisfies neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test — not '3 or more flags', and not the 0.05 ratio with at least 40 trips. Those two fields are the only ones POL-RD-06 permits for this test, and neither supports escalation to the FULL_REFUND remedy or the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral; the rider's remedy stays at the POL-RD-02 partial figure of 8.05.

The rider authorised the diversion as it happened. The chat log records the driver messaging at 18:22:40, two minutes into the trip, that the Pelton Canal Link closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop, and the rider replying at 18:23:10, 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion' — an instruction from the rider, in the chat log, inside the three minutes after the vehicle left the optimal corridor that POL-RD-04 allows. I disclose that the rider named no road and the message carries no waypoint_hint, so the 200 m waypoint-corroboration limb of POL-RD-04 cannot be run on this record; the exchange is relied on as the rider's authorisation of the diversion the driver had just identified, which is why the industrial-loop routing cannot be treated as the driver's unilateral choice.

The driver has discharged the burden POL-RD-08 places on him once the rider shows an excess: he points to a specific artifact and a specific clause — traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 and POL-RD-03 — rather than a general assertion that traffic was bad. The advisory names the road, carries an ID, overlaps the trip window and matches a route that leaves and rejoins the optimal corridor, which is exactly what POL-RD-08 requires. The excess is also stable and admissible: the governing figure is the trace distance of 18.0 km under POL-RD-01, the trace is at full weight with no gaps, so the 3.60 km cap does not move and the rider cannot inflate the measured excess beyond it.
